Does observed-upper velocity improve density predictions?

One controlled change: add 29 observed-upper u slots and 29 v slots to the 38-feature baseline. Keep both VID thresholds at 6.6/6.6, all 1,446,106 training profiles, sampled targets, weights, splits and hyperparameters unchanged. Velocities remain in m/s; missing values remain missing. All density and velocity inputs are at or above the observed edge.

The model selected 12,107 rounds from a 20,000-round ceiling, using mean raw-density stopping RMSE at 100–500 m. Density is still the only prediction target.

Result: mean RMSE fell by 7.4% on historical reporting nights, 7.2% in the held-out year, 4.6% at unseen sites and 4.3% at unseen sites in the held-out year. All four evaluations improved at 200–500 m; 100 m slightly worsened at unseen sites.

Interpretation and reproduction

These are paired scores on identical examples; each depth is one hidden layer. Improvement can reflect movement information and velocity-availability/quality cues. One fit does not quantify seed variability, and these repeatedly inspected holdouts are development evaluations. Artificially withheld measured bins do not directly validate naturally missing near-ground layers.

The paired-profile and held-out-profile tabs use this selected u/v model, retaining their existing examples and five-bin limits. Feature importance describes the same selected trees. Historical threshold comparisons remain unchanged.
